text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- What we must do within the next year is to provide Bosnia with a new governing framework and parliament needs to adopt a series of laws, Michael Steiner, deputy to international High Representative Carl Bildt, says in interview.
- Bosnian politicians regard U.S. President Bill Clinton as key figure for peace in Bosnia, newspaper survey shows.
- Bosnian economic expert Dragoljub Stojanov says proposal to let demobilised soldiers buy flats with their bank books could have "unforseeable economic and political consequences."
- Any solution that gives Moslems a right to return and live in Brcko will be acceptable, town's mayor in exile Munib Jusufovic says before upcoming third arbitration session in Rome on January 8-10.
- Sources close to newspaper say a Croat will be candidate for post of president of the Croat-Moslem Federation while candidate for deputy post will again be Ejup Ganic, a Moslem.
- Director of Sarajevo car producer TAS, Husein Musabegovic, asks Bosnian government to ban import of second-hand cars to Croat-Moslem Federation.
